M1-F01.summary: export writes a category that holds a comma, a double quote, or a line break as it is, so the CSV line splits into the wrong columns or rows
M1-F01.fixed_when: every category comes back unchanged when the export is read as CSV, for example a category `eat, out` added on 2026-09-03 exports as `2026-09-03,"eat, out",2.00`

M1-F02.summary: add accepts a negative amount: `add food -5` records -5.00 and lowers the food total
M1-F02.last_evidence: add food -5 -> added -5.00 to food; total food -> Total food: -5.00
M1-F02.fixed_when: `add food -5` exits 2 with an error and records nothing, and `add food 0` is still accepted

M1-F03.summary: an unreadable expenses.json is read as an empty list, so `add` overwrites it with one expense (L-01) and total, export, and archive show nothing (I-D2)
M1-F03.last_evidence: printf '{broken' > expenses.json; add food 1 -> exit 0; expenses.json now holds one expense
M1-F03.fixed_when: with expenses.json holding `{broken`, `add food 1` exits 2 with an error naming the file and the file still holds `{broken`; total, export, and archive refuse it the same way
